sources.title: codex-action README.md
sources.locator: Introduction; Pull Request Bot; Inputs; Permission profiles; Safety Strategy; Outputs; Azure
sources.finding: Composite GitHub Action installs Codex and a Responses API proxy; caller supplies provider API key. Workflow prompt/file and model/effort inputs configure codex exec. GitHub workflow handles triggers, checkout and subsequent publishing.

sources.title: codex-action docs/security.md
sources.locator: Limiting who can run; Limit command permissions; Protecting API key
sources.finding: Default callers need repository write access, with explicit allowlists for additional actors/bots. Permission profiles limit commands separately from process privilege reduction; drop-sudo and unprivileged-user have distinct runner requirements.

sources.title: codex-action LICENSE
sources.finding: Action source is Apache License 2.0 at pinned revision; Codex and provider/runner terms are separate.

sources.title: codex-action Default-branch commit
sources.finding: Pinned default-branch commit dated 30 October 2026; release API returned no releases in this pass.

sources.title: codex-action README
sources.finding: Users must supply an API key for their chosen provider (OpenAI or Azure OpenAI) as a GitHub secret, so model usage is billed by that provider; no price for the action is stated.

sources.title: codex-action LICENSE
sources.locator: Apache License 2.0, section 2 (Grant of Copyright License)
sources.finding: The Apache-2.0 license grants a perpetual, no-charge, royalty-free copyright licence to use and redistribute the software.

sources.title: Codex Action README: API key requirement
sources.finding: Users must provide an API key for their chosen provider, such as OPENAI_API_KEY or AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY, as a GitHub Actions secret to use this action.

sources.title: Codex Action entry point and runtime boundary
sources.locator: Entire composite action, inputs and outputs; src/main.ts command registration; src/runCodexExec.ts:255-355; package.json
sources.finding: The composite action installs only Codex and its Responses proxy, runs one codex exec process on the selected runner, and returns a final message. Its helper CLI has action setup/run commands. Inspection of action.yml and src found no desktop/browser/mobile client, harness adapter, agent delegation controller, task database, shared-prompt server, SSO, diff viewer, PR creation, worktree/container/VM provisioning or action telemetry toggle. GitHub supplies workflow control and permissions; Codex internals are separate.

sources.title: GitHub Actions concurrency
sources.finding: GitHub Actions permits jobs and multiple instances of a workflow to run concurrently by default; caller concurrency settings and runner quotas can restrict this.
